```{=html}
<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Appendix B <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Proofs &amp; Comments</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">B.4</span> Curves realizing the vector space operations of <span class="math inline">\(T_p\mathcal{M}\)</span> (§<a class="dg-xref" href="../tangent-spaces/tangent-space.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Tangent_Space">4.1</a>)</h1></header>
<p>In Section <a class="dg-xref" href="../tangent-spaces/tangent-space.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Tangent_Space">4.1</a> we defined the tangent space <span class="math inline">\(T_p\mathcal{M}\)</span> at a point <span class="math inline">\(p \in \mathcal{M}\)</span> as the collection of velocity linear maps associated with smooth curves passing through <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>. The algebraic structure of <span class="math inline">\(T_p\mathcal{M}\)</span> as a real vector space was introduced by endowing it with the operations of addition and s-multiplication, defined operationally via their action on smooth functions <span class="math inline">\(f \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span>: <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
    (v_{\gamma_1, p} \oplus_T v_{\gamma_2, p})(f) &amp;\coloneqq v_{\gamma_1, p}(f) + v_{\gamma_2, p}(f), \\
    (\alpha \odot_T v_{\gamma, p})(f)             &amp;\coloneqq \alpha \cdot v_{\gamma, p}(f).
\end{align*}</span> While these definitions correctly encode the vector space axioms, an important subtlety arises from the fact that each tangent vector is itself defined via the velocity of some smooth curve passing through <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>. Therefore, to guarantee that <span class="math inline">\(T_p\mathcal{M}\)</span> is closed under <span class="math inline">\(\oplus_T\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\odot_T\)</span>—that is, that the result of these operations still corresponds to the velocity of a smooth curve passing through <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>—it is necessary to demonstrate that such curves indeed exist. In other words, we must prove the following:</p>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p>For any two smooth curves <span class="math inline">\(\gamma_1\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\gamma_2\)</span> passing through <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>, there exists a third smooth curve <span class="math inline">\(\sigma\)</span> whose velocity satisfies <span class="math inline">\(v_{\sigma, p} = v_{\gamma_1, p} \oplus_T v_{\gamma_2, p}.\)</span></p></li>
<li><p>For any smooth curve <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> passing through <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> and any real scalar <span class="math inline">\(\alpha \in \mathbb{R}\)</span>, there exists a smooth curve <span class="math inline">\({\sigma}\)</span> whose velocity satisfies <span class="math inline">\(v_{{\sigma}, p} = \alpha \odot_T v_{\gamma, p}.\)</span></p></li>
</ul>
<p>This appendix provides a constructive proof of these facts:</p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li><p>To prove the existence of a smooth curve realizing the addition operation <span class="math inline">\(v_{\gamma_1, p} \oplus_T v_{\gamma_2, p}\)</span> for two tangent vectors <span class="math inline">\(v_{\gamma_1, p}, v_{\gamma_2, p} \in T_p\mathcal{M}\)</span>, we proceed as follows.</p>
<p>Let <span class="math inline">\(\gamma_1, \gamma_2 : \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow \mathcal{M}\)</span> be two smooth curves passing through <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>, i.e., there exist parameters <span class="math inline">\(\lambda_1, \lambda_2 \in \mathbb{R}\)</span> such that <span class="math inline">\(\gamma_1(\lambda_1) = \gamma_2(\lambda_2) = p\)</span>.</p>
<p>We construct a new curve <span class="math inline">\(\sigma_{\mathscr{X}} : \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow \mathcal{M}\)</span>, defined in terms of a local chart <span class="math inline">\(\left(\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X}\right)\)</span> with <span class="math inline">\(p \in \mathcal{U}\)</span>, as follows:  <span class="math display">\begin{align}
            \sigma_{\mathscr{X}}(\lambda) := \mathscr{X}^{-1}
            \big[ (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1)(\lambda_1 + \lambda) + (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_2)(\lambda_2 + \lambda) - (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1)(\lambda_1) \big]  =... \tag{B.1}\\
            ... = \mathscr{X}^{-1}
            \big[ (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_1)(\lambda) + (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_2 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_2)(\lambda) - (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\varnothing)(\lambda) \big]=... \tag{B.2}\\
            ... = \mathscr{X}^{-1}
            \big[ \big( (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_1) + (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_2 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_2) - (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\varnothing)\big) \big] (\lambda). \tag{B.3}
        \end{align}</span>  Where we have defined the reparametrization functions  <span class="math display">\[
            \begin{aligned}
                &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                    \begin{aligned}
                        \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_1 \colon \mathbb{R} &amp;\longrightarrow \mathbb{R} \\
                        \lambda &amp;\longmapsto \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_1(\lambda) \coloneqq \lambda + \lambda_1
                    \end{aligned}
                \end{array}
                \quad
                &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                    \begin{aligned}
                        \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_2 \colon \mathbb{R} &amp;\longrightarrow \mathbb{R} \\
                        \lambda                               &amp;\longmapsto \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_2(\lambda) \coloneqq \lambda + \lambda_2
                    \end{aligned}
                \end{array}
                \quad
                &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                    \begin{aligned}
                        \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\varnothing \colon \mathbb{R} &amp;\longrightarrow \mathbb{R} \\
                        \lambda &amp;\longmapsto \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\varnothing(\lambda) \coloneqq \lambda_1
                    \end{aligned}
                \end{array}
            \end{aligned}
        \]</span>  This construction corresponds, in local coordinates, to performing a vector addition of the coordinate representations of the curves’ increments around the point <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>. It is immediate to verify that <span class="math inline">\(\sigma(0) = p\)</span>.</p>
<p>Now applying the multidimensional chain rule (check the footnote in subsection <a class="dg-xref" href="../tangent-spaces/tangent-space.html#subsection_Basis_and_Coordinate_Components_of_TpM" data-kind="subsection" data-label="subsection_Basis_and_Coordinate_Components_of_TpM">4.1.1</a>) forwards and then backwards:  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            v_{\sigma_{\mathscr{X}}, p}(f)
            &amp;:= (f \circ \sigma_{\mathscr{X}})'(0)
            = \left( f \circ (\mathscr{X}^{-1} \circ \mathscr{X}) \circ \sigma_{\mathscr{X}} \right)'(0)
            = \left( (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \circ (\mathscr{X} \circ \sigma_{\mathscr{X}}) \right)'(0) \\
            &amp;= \sum_{i} \left\lbrace
            \left[ (\mathscr{X} \circ \sigma_{\mathscr{X}})_i \right]'(0)
            \cdot
            \partial_i (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \big( \mathscr{X}(p) \big)
            \right\rbrace \\
            &amp;= \sum_{i} \left\lbrace
            \left[ (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_1)_i'(0)
            + (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_2 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_2)_i'(0)
            - (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\varnothing)_i'(0) \right]
            \cdot
            \partial_i (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \big( \mathscr{X}(p) \big)
            \right\rbrace \\
            &amp;= \sum_{i} \left\lbrace
            \left[ (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1)_i'(\lambda_1)
            + (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_2)_i'(\lambda_2) \right]
            \cdot
            \partial_i (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \big( \mathscr{X}(p) \big)
            \right\rbrace \\
            &amp;= \sum_{i} \left\lbrace
            (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1)_i'(\lambda_1)
            \cdot \partial_i (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \big( \mathscr{X}(p) \big)
            + (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_2)_i'(\lambda_2)
            \cdot \partial_i (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \big( \mathscr{X}(p) \big)
            \right\rbrace \\
            &amp;= \left( (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \circ (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1) \right)'(\lambda_1)
            + \left( (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \circ (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_2) \right)'(\lambda_2) \\
            &amp;= \left( f \circ (\mathscr{X}^{-1} \circ \mathscr{X}) \circ \gamma_1 \right)'(\lambda_1)
            + \left( f \circ (\mathscr{X}^{-1} \circ \mathscr{X}) \circ \gamma_2 \right)'(\lambda_2) \\
            &amp;= (f \circ \gamma_1)'(\lambda_1) + (f \circ \gamma_2)'(\lambda_2) \\
            &amp;= v_{\gamma_1, p}(f) + v_{\gamma_2, p}(f).
        \end{align*}</span>  which confirms that the curve <span class="math inline">\(\sigma\)</span> realizes the tangent vector <span class="math inline">\(v_{\gamma_1, p} \oplus_T v_{\gamma_2, p}\)</span> according to the operational definition of addition in the tangent space <span class="math inline">\(T_p\mathcal{M}\)</span>.</p>
<p>As anticipated, while the construction was carried out using a local chart, the resulting tangent vector is independent of the chosen chart, since the final expression for the velocity depends only on derivatives evaluated at <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>, which transform covariantly under chart transitions.</p></li>
<li><p>To prove the existence of a smooth curve realizing the scalar multiplication operation <span class="math inline">\(\alpha \odot_T v_{\gamma, p}\)</span> for a given tangent vector <span class="math inline">\(v_{\gamma, p} \in T_p\mathcal{M}\)</span> and scalar <span class="math inline">\(\alpha \in \mathbb{R}\)</span>, we proceed as follows.</p>
<p>Let <span class="math inline">\(\gamma : \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow \mathcal{M}\)</span> be any smooth curve passing through <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>, i.e., such that <span class="math inline">\(\exists \lambda_1 \in \mathbb{R}\)</span> with <span class="math inline">\(\gamma(\lambda_1) = p\)</span>. We construct the reparametrized curve <span class="math inline">\({\sigma} : \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow \mathcal{M}\)</span> as:  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            {\sigma}(\lambda) \coloneqq \gamma\big(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha(\lambda)\big)
            = (\gamma \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha)(\lambda),
        \end{align*}</span>  where the reparametrization function <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha\)</span> is defined by:  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha : \mathbb{R} &amp;\longrightarrow \mathbb{R} \\
            \lambda                               &amp;\longmapsto \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha(\lambda) \coloneqq \alpha\lambda + \lambda_1.
        \end{align*}</span>  It is immediate to verify that <span class="math inline">\({\sigma}(0) = \gamma(\lambda_1) = p\)</span>, so <span class="math inline">\({\sigma}\)</span> is indeed a curve passing through <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>.</p>
<p>Now, applying the chain rule for the composition of smooth functions, we compute the velocity of <span class="math inline">\({\sigma}\)</span> at <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> with respect to any smooth function <span class="math inline">\(f \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span>:  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            v_{\sigma, p}(f)
            &amp;\coloneqq (f \circ {\sigma})'(0)
            = \frac{d}{d\lambda}\Big|_{\lambda=0} (f \circ \gamma \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha)(\lambda) = ...\\
            ...&amp; = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha'(0) \cdot (f \circ \gamma)'(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha(0))
            = \alpha \cdot (f \circ \gamma)'(\lambda_1)
            = \alpha \cdot v_{\gamma, p}(f).
        \end{align*}</span>  This shows that the curve <span class="math inline">\({\sigma}\)</span> realizes the scalar multiple <span class="math inline">\(\alpha \odot_T v_{\gamma, p}\)</span> according to the operational definition of scalar multiplication in the tangent space <span class="math inline">\(T_p\mathcal{M}\)</span>.</p></li>
</ol>

```
